name: Arcturus Defense Solutions PhantomNet EW-6 Electronic Warfar
description:
The PhantomNet EW-6 is Arcturus Defense Solutions' dedicated electronic warfare BCI, purpose-built for signals intelligence operators, cyber-warfare specialists, and ECM field units operating in contested electromagnetic environments. The unit integrates a six-channel spectral analysis co-processor with direct neural interfacing, enabling the operator to perceive the electromagnetic spectrum as a fully navigable sensory space — hostile comms traffic, drone guidance frequencies, automated turret control signals, and encrypted military uplinks become as legible as visual terrain to a trained EW-6 operator. Active countermeasure suites allow direct neural-initiated jamming across designated frequency bands, while the unit's proprietary ShadowWeave spoofing architecture can generate convincing false electromagnetic signatures to misdirect autonomous targeting systems. The full-skull Faraday mesh is rated to MIL-SPEC EMP-11, the highest civilian-accessible rating, and the unit's own emissions are suppressed to below ambient noise floor during passive operation.

Electronic warfare operators running the EW-6 occupy a peculiar cultural niche within Meridian 88's military structure — simultaneously indispensable and deeply mistrusted. The ability to perceive and manipulate invisible signal architectures is regarded by conventional infantry with a suspicion that borders on superstition; EW-6 operators are commonly called 'Phantoms' or 'Ghosters' in field vernacular, and are often billeted separately from standard units. Several high-profile incidents in which EW-6 operators were found to have been passively intercepting command-level communications — officially for tactical purposes — have generated ongoing classified reviews within the Meridian 88 Strategic Command, though no formal charges have ever been filed.
installation_requirements: Level 5 neuro-surgical facility; ADS EW-certified neurotechnician; full-skull Faraday mesh installation mandatory; spectral co-processor requires 96-hour neural mapping calibration; psychological clearance per ADS EW Directive 12-F
rejection_risk: Low (5%); risk elevates significantly with prior cochlear or auditory augmentation due to spectral co-processor interference
maintenance: Monthly firmware updates via ADS secure channel mandatory; spectral array recalibration every 6 months; ShadowWeave spoofing library updated quarterly via encrypted ADS depot uplink

side_effects: Electromagnetic synesthesia: passive spectral perception bleeds into waking consciousness, causing ordinary electrical infrastructure — lighting grids, transit systems, civilian comms — to register as intrusive noise or visual static overlays
Frequency fixation episodes: operators become involuntarily locked onto a detected signal, unable to disengage conscious attention for periods of 30 seconds to several minutes

Interpersonal trust erosion: chronic passive interception of ambient communications produces a documented psychological pattern of hypervigilant suspicion toward unaugmented individuals whose communications cannot be monitored
Tinnitus-variant phantom carrier tones: persistent low-amplitude tonal experiences corresponding to no real-world signal source, reported by 67% of long-term EW-6 operators
cultural_context: The EW-6 and its operators exist in a space that the broader military culture finds uncomfortable — the ability to silently surveil and disrupt communications systems sits at an uneasy intersection of tactical necessity and potential betrayal. Within intelligence and cyber-warfare communities, EW-6 operators are regarded as elite practitioners of an almost esoteric discipline; outside those communities, they are regarded with the particular unease reserved for those who can listen to conversations no one intended to share. The street mythology around black-market EW-6 units — allegedly modified to remove ADS usage logging — sustains a thriving underground of corporate espionage speculation.
known_users: Rumored use by at least two major corporate intelligence divisions operating under military contractor cover
story_hooks: An EW-6 operator on a routine signals sweep begins detecting an encrypted carrier frequency that matches no known military or civilian protocol — the signal is broadcasting from beneath the city, from infrastructure that has been sealed since the Collapse of 2187.

A PhantomNet unit is recovered from a killed enemy operative, and its ShadowWeave spoofing library contains false electromagnetic signatures for vessels and installations that technically do not exist — including one that matches the players' current base of operations.

A veteran EW-6 operator is being quietly retired by ADS, their unit scheduled for mandatory wipe and reissue. They have three days to prove that what they've been intercepting in their involuntary frequency-fixation episodes is real intelligence and not a symptom of system degradation.
